listen_text: Section. Soundness of Natural Deduction. We will now prove soundness of natural deduction with regards to the relational semantics, that is, showing that if a formula is derivable from a set of assumptions then the set of assumptions entails the formula. Theorem. Soundness. If A is derivable from Gamma , then Gamma entails A . End theorem. Proof. We prove that if A is derivable from Gamma , then Gamma entails A . The proof is by induction on the derivation of A from Gamma . List. Next item. If the derivation consists of just the assumption A , we have A is derivable from A , and want to show that A entails A . Suppose that model M satisfies A at world w . Then trivially model M satisfies A at world w . Next item. The derivation ends in conjunction introduction : Exercise. Next item. The derivation ends in conjunction elimination : Exercise. Next item. The derivation ends in disjunction introduction : Suppose the premise is B , and the undischarged assumptions of the derivation ending in B are Gamma . Then we have B is derivable from Gamma and by inductive hypothesis, Gamma entails B . We have to show that Gamma entails the disjunction B or C . Suppose model M satisfies every formula in Gamma at world w . Since Gamma entails B , model M satisfies B at world w . But then also model M satisfies the disjunction B or C at world w . Similarly, if the premise is C , we have that Gamma entails C . Next item. The derivation ends in disjunction elimination : The derivations ending in the premises are of B or C from undischarged assumptions Gamma , of D from undischarged assumptions Delta subscript one union the singleton containing B , and of D from undischarged assumptions Delta subscript two union the singleton containing C . So we have the disjunction B or C is derivable from Gamma , D is derivable from Delta subscript one together with B , and D is derivable from Delta subscript two together with C . By induction hypothesis, Gamma entails the disjunction B or C , Delta subscript one together with B entails D , and Delta subscript two together with C entails D . We have to prove that Gamma union Delta subscript one union Delta subscript two entails D . Suppose model M satisfies every formula in Gamma union Delta subscript one union Delta subscript two at world w . Then model M satisfies every formula in Gamma at world w and since Gamma entails the disjunction B or C , model M satisfies the disjunction B or C at world w . By definition of satisfaction in model M , either model M satisfies B at world w or model M satisfies C at world w . So we distinguish cases: (a) model M satisfies B at world w . Then model M satisfies every formula in Delta subscript one together with B at world w . Since Delta subscript one together with B entails D , we have model M satisfies D at world w . (b) model M satisfies C at world w . Then model M satisfies every formula in Delta subscript two together with C at world w . Since Delta subscript two together with C entails D , we have model M satisfies D at world w . So in either case, model M satisfies D at world w , as we wanted to show. Disclosed reader correction. listen_text: Section. Lindenbaum's Lemma. The completeness theorem for intuitionistic logic is proved by assuming A is not derivable from Gamma and constructing a model every formula in Gamma is true throughout model M and A is not true throughout model M . In classical logic the relation of derivability can be reduced to the notion of consistency since a formula A is derivable from a set of formulas if and only if the set together with the negation of A is inconsistent. This is not possible in intuitionistic logic. In intuitionistic logic, if not A is inconsistent, we only get that double negation of A is derivable without assumptions . Since if not not A then A does not hold intuitionistically in general, we cannot conclude that A is derivable without assumptions . Thus, when constructing the model model M , we will need to keep track of the non-derivability of the formula A and thus we will not be able to use a complete set Gamma star contains Gamma to build the model model M , as in every complete set Gamma star , we have A or not A is derivable from Gamma star . Instead of using a complete set Gamma star , we will us the notion of a prime set of formulas: Definition. A set of formulas Gamma is prime if and only if List. Next item. Gamma is consistent, that is, falsity is not derivable from Gamma ; Next item. if A is derivable from Gamma then A belongs to Gamma ; and Next item. if A or B belongs to Gamma then A belongs to Gamma or B belongs to Gamma . End list. End definition. Lemma. Lindenbaum's Lemma. If A is not derivable from Gamma , there is a Gamma star contains Gamma such that Gamma star is prime and A is not derivable from Gamma star . End lemma. Proof. Let B subscript one or C subscript one , B subscript two or C subscript two , and so on, be an enumeration of all formulas of the form B or C . We'll define an increasing sequence of sets of formulas Gamma subscript n , where each Gamma subscript n plus one is defined as Gamma subscript n together with one new formula. Gamma star will be the union of all Gamma subscript n . The new formulas are selected so as to ensure that Gamma star is prime and still A is not derivable from Gamma star . This means that at each step we should find the first disjunction B subscript i or C subscript i such that: List. Next item. B subscript i or C subscript i is derivable from Gamma subscript n Next item. B subscript i does not belong to Gamma subscript n and C subscript i does not belong to Gamma subscript n End list. listen_text: Section. The Completeness Theorem. Theorem. If Gamma entails A then A is derivable from Gamma . End theorem. Proof. We prove the contrapositive: Suppose A is not derivable from Gamma . Then by Lindenbaum's Lemma , there is a prime set Gamma star contains Gamma such that A is not derivable from Gamma star . Consider the canonical model canonical model M of Gamma star for Gamma star as defined in the definition of the canonical model . For any B belongs to Gamma , B is derivable from Gamma star . Note that Gamma star of the empty sequence equals Gamma star . By the Truth Lemma ( the Truth Lemma ), we have model M of Gamma star satisfies B at the empty sequence for all B belongs to Gamma and model M of Gamma star does not satisfy A at the empty sequence . This shows that Gamma does not entail A . End proof. Exercise. Show that if A only contains propositional variables, disjunction , and conjunction , then A is not valid . Use this to conclude that conditional is not definable in intuitionistic logic from disjunction and conjunction . End exercise. This exercise remains unsolved. Exercise. (Hint: Assume A is not true throughout model M subscript one and B is not true throughout model M subscript two and construct a new model model M such that A or B is not true throughout model M .) End exercise. This exercise remains unsolved. Exercise. Show that if model M is a relational model using a linear order then either if A then B, or if B then A, is true throughout model M .
